flashcard_questions.q: Which line does Macbeth speak first in the play, echoing the witches?
flashcard_questions.a: ‘So foul and fair a day I have not seen.’

flashcard_questions.q: Which chant from Act 1, Scene 1 does Macbeth unknowingly echo?
flashcard_questions.a: ‘Fair is foul, and foul is fair.’

flashcard_questions.q: Which title does Ross announce Macbeth has been given in Act 1, Scene 3?
Who warns Macbeth that ‘the instruments of darkness tell us truths’ in order to betray?
Which prophecy tells Banquo his descendants will rule although he never will?
flashcard_questions.a: ‘Thou shalt get kings, though thou be none.’

flashcard_questions.q: Why does Shakespeare make Banquo the father of a royal line?
flashcard_questions.a: To flatter King James I, who believed he was descended from Banquo.

flashcard_questions.q: Which aside shows Macbeth deciding to leave the crown to chance?
flashcard_questions.a: ‘If chance will have me king, why, chance may crown me, without my stir.’

flashcard_questions.q: What does Macbeth mean by calling his thought of murder ‘but fantastical’?
flashcard_questions.a: The killing exists only in his imagination, yet it already shakes him.

flashcard_questions.q: Which image shows Macbeth hiding his ambition from heaven in Act 1, Scene 4?
flashcard_questions.a: ‘Stars, hide your fires; let not light see my black and deep desires.’

flashcard_questions.q: Who does Duncan name as Prince of Cumberland and heir to the throne?
What is hamartia in a tragedy?
flashcard_questions.a: A fatal flaw in the tragic hero’s character that leads to their downfall.

flashcard_questions.q: Which flaw in Macbeth’s character drives him towards his downfall?
What is a foil in drama?
flashcard_questions.a: A character who contrasts with another to highlight that character’s qualities.

flashcard_questions.q: Which line of Duncan’s shows he cannot read treachery in a face?
flashcard_questions.a: ‘There’s no art to find the mind’s construction in the face.’

flashcard_questions.q: What does dramatic irony mean in a play?
flashcard_questions.a: The audience knows something a character on stage does not.

notes: 15 cards: 6 quotation-recall fronts (first line, witches’ chant, chance aside, ‘Stars, hide your fires’, Banquo’s prophecy, Duncan’s ‘no art’ line), 2 quotation-to-effect (‘but fantastical’, hamartia), 1 quotation-to-speaker (Banquo’s warning), 1 context-to-relevance (James I descent), 2 plot-fact naming (Cawdor, Malcolm), 3 term-to-definition (hamartia, foil, dramatic irony). Dropped ‘witches’, ‘incantation’ and ‘ambiguous’ as glossary flavour; ‘incantation’ and ‘ambiguous’ would interfere with the term cards kept. All quotations copied verbatim from the lesson content.
